Does the order of rejection matter?
1 tried

No. Run test and Step choose, at each step, the hypothesis whose p-value is smallest compared with its level, but any order you choose ends with the same rejections (Bretz et al., 2009).

With these p-values the hypotheses can be rejected in 2 different orders, and every one of them ends with the same result: H1, H2, H3 rejected.

Order tried	Rejected at the end
H1 → H2 → H3
Run test / Step	H1, H2, H3

3 steps
Rejected H1: p = 0.004 ≤ 1/2 × 0.025 = 0.0125.

Weights now: H2 3/4 (level 0.01875), H3 1/4 (level 0.00625), H4 0 (level 0).
Rejected H2: p = 0.009 ≤ 3/4 × 0.025 = 0.01875.
Passed on: +1/4 to H3, +1/2 to H4.
Weights now: H3 1/2 (level 0.0125), H4 1/2 (level 0.0125).
Rejected H3: p = 0.011 ≤ 1/2 × 0.025 = 0.0125.
Passed on: +1/2 to H4.
Weights now: H4 1 (level 0.025).
Stopped: no remaining hypothesis has p ≤ its local level. Not rejected: H4.
